feedback: Before this geometry races, the evidence is as follows. In iteration 0 (60 trials, zero completions), every run ended off track at max_error about 0.062 m with about one line-loss event per run. In iteration 1, the seven-sensor, 16 mm, y = 0.03 m array removed line loss (oval, s-bend and slalom all at 0) but max_error stayed at 0.0619 m, so sensing was fixed and tracking lag remained. Iteration 1 also showed that moving the row to y = 0.03 m cut oval steering_oscillation from 0.245 to 0.173, while slalom was unchanged at about 0.14. Progress fell from 0.42 to 0.31 on the oval, so speed or the agility of the drivetrain may now be limiting. To work with this geometry I narrowed the controller gains: a 0.09 m track gives about 33% more yaw per command, so I reduced kp to 2.5 and raised kd to 0.4. Next race, if max_error drops below 0.06 m, keep the agility and tune further. If max_error stays near 0.062 m with oscillation low, the reaction point is the limit: try moving the row forward to y = 0.02 m or 0.04 m. If oscillation rises above about 0.2 on the oval, the track is too narrow for the gains: widen it back toward 0.10 m.
requested_changes: If max_error stays near 0.062 m with line_loss_events at 0 and steering_oscillation below about 0.2: keep wheel_track 0.09 m and mass 0.6 kg, and test wheel_radius 0.035 m to recover progress, since iteration 1 fell from 0.42 to 0.31 on the oval with no line loss.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 on the oval (iteration 1 was 0.173 and iteration 0 was 0.245) after this race: widen wheel_track to 0.10 m to lower yaw gain per command, because the narrower track raised yaw response by about 33%.

If max_error stays at 0.062 m with the narrower track and oscillation is already low: move the sensor row to y = 0.02 m, because iteration 1 showed y = 0.03 m reduced oval oscillation (0.245 to 0.173) without changing max_error, so the reaction point, not the sensors, is the next lever.
